clue.text: Neglectful of duty, Quentin led astray

indicators.note: led astray means led off the right path, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A boy called Quentin has been led into bad ways and stopped doing what he should.
explanation.definitionFit: A delinquent person fails in an obligation; the adjective describes someone remiss about responsibilities.

clue.text: Deny any connection with small island situated within NI county

indicators.note: something situated within another sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland
IS is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone renounces a tiny islet that lies inside a Northern Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland; Down is one of its counties.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge any relationship with a person or thing, as a parent might a child.

clue.text: Sad songs, last to be broadcast about soldiers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged word wraps around the other piece
broadcasting scatters something widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the word itself is the material to be rearranged
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: A radio station saves its saddest songs, about soldiers, to be played at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like an instruction about order, but it is just the four letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Laments are mournful songs or poems expressing grief, so sad songs is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Italian girl giving support to former PM in a state

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece giving support sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence
an Italian form of the girl's name Caroline

explanation.surface: An Italian woman lends her backing to an ex-prime minister in some unnamed country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the supporting piece is placed below, so the girl's name follows the PM's.
explanation.definitionFit: North Carolina is one of the fifty United States, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Dickens character — one with a bit of humour, he appears in Peru after revolution

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be placed inside it
a revolution turns something around, so the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: the South American country
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of humour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dickensian figure with a touch of wit turns up in Peru after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising in Peru, but it means the country's name turns round; the four letters before it then sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is the fawning, 'umble clerk who schemes against Mr Wickfield in David Copperfield.

clue.text: A street in New York that's filthy

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for New York
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A grimy Manhattan street is the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty can mean dirty or disgusting, as in a nasty smell, so it matches filthy.

clue.text: Old garment, article obtained on the way back

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: the indefinite article
got means obtained

explanation.surface: An item of clothing from the past is picked up on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition: the garment is Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose draped outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Direct extra to spot

parts.note: over means in excess, as in money left over
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: An instruction to send an additional person to a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' reads as a verb about sending someone, but it is the verb meaning supervise.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee work is to supervise or manage it, which is what directing it means.

clue.text: Fighting a lawsuit

definitions.meaning: second meaning: legal proceedings brought in court

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like someone contesting a lawsuit, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Action means military combat and also a legal case brought against someone, as in a libel action.

clue.text: Warrior in SA painting, unfinished one

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a mural is a painting on a wall
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fighter is depicted in a half-finished South African artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: SA suggests South Africa, but the two letters are used just as they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of the hereditary military class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: National issue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a citizen of a country
second meaning: a topic under discussion

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a matter of national importance, but 'National' is a noun for a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is a person owing allegiance to a state, and also the matter being discussed.

clue.text: See writer boot out vacuous young man-about-town

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the three words supply all the letters

explanation.surface: An order to watch an author kick out an empty-headed idler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot out' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'boot' is fodder and 'out' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie Wooster is P G Wodehouse's amiable, dim-witted rich bachelor, a classic idle man about town.

clue.text: Girl in very large city church

parts.note: the Great Wen was Cobbett's name for London, so a wen is a huge city
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A young woman is found inside a big city's church.
explanation.walkthrough: A wen is literally a cyst; William Cobbett called sprawling London 'the Great Wen', and setters use wen for any overgrown city.
explanation.definitionFit: Wench is an old or jocular word for a young woman, especially a country girl or serving maid.

clue.text: The osprey's adapted — that's the trick!

indicators.note: something adapted is altered to suit, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A bird of prey has evolved, and someone hails the result as the knack.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is the conjuror's exclamation as a trick is completed, announcing the magic has worked.

clue.text: Mountain shop's first around to cut down on fish

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of shop
CA is circa, Latin for around, used with dates
to fell a tree is to cut it down
the pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A shop is told to start cutting back its fish stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Scafell Pike, in the Lake District, is England's highest mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Scafell Pike is a peak in Cumbria and the highest summit in England.

clue.text: Left vessel nearby to indulge in horseplay

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Noah's ark is a vessel
about means near, as in somewhere about here

explanation.surface: A boat abandoned close at hand becomes a place for rough play.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to fool around boisterously, which is exactly what horseplay means.

clue.text: Bird, wren, was flying round ring

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
letters that are flying are scattered about and land in a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A wren is seen flying in circles around a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wren' looks like the bird defined, but it is fodder; the definition is the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The whooper swan is a large wild swan with a yellow-and-black bill, named for its loud call.

clue.text: Current of air well above river Thames town

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece placed above comes earlier in the answer

parts.note: wind is moving air
so and well both open a sentence, as in so, what now
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A breeze blows over a riverside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Windsor, home of Windsor Castle, stands on the Thames west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is a Berkshire town on the River Thames, famous for its royal castle.

clue.text: Jotter found in flat underneath record

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece underneath goes lower, so it comes second

parts.note: to note something is to record it
pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A notebook turns up in an apartment beneath a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small book of paper for quick notes, the same thing as a notepad.

clue.text: Modest tea set out

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: set out suggests laying things out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A demure tea service has been laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea set' looks like one item, but the words are split between a synonym and anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and decorous in behaviour, which overlaps with modest in the sense of decent.

clue.text: Piece of sponge eaten by timid type for dessert

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside whoever eats it

parts.note: a mousy person is shy and timid

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of sponge

explanation.surface: A shy person nibbles a slice of sponge cake for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' and 'dessert' together suggest cake, but only the first letter of sponge is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light, airy sweet dish made with whipped cream or egg whites.

clue.text: I threaten naughty girl

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters will not stay in line

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: An adult warns a disobedient girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrietta is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Tabloid's leader, article on good round dance

indicators.note: the leader is whatever comes at the front, here the opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of tabloid
the indefinite article
G is the abbreviation for good
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tabloid editorial piece about a ballroom dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance of Argentine origin with gliding steps and sharp pauses.

clue.text: Better public function

parts.note: once news is out it is public
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: An improved civic event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To better someone is to surpass them, and outdo means exactly that.

clue.text: Spot inhabited by American bear

indicators.note: a place inhabited by someone has them living inside it

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark
US for American

explanation.surface: A place where an American bear lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' reads as the animal, but it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a loss or a weight is to bear it, either endure it or hold it up.

clue.text: Old copper's shown holding head of sea creature

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something holding another has it gripped inside

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the head of something is its top
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: An elderly policeman is shown gripping a sea creature's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman (COP), but it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: The octopus is an eight-armed marine mollusc, a classic creature of the sea.

clue.text: Organ — new make

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A church organ of the latest make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' reads as a brand, but it is the verb, as in make a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to make it through work, as in making a fortune.

clue.text: 12in. spanner unsuitable for the motorist?

parts.note: twelve inches make a foot
a bridge spans a gap

explanation.surface: A twelve-inch wrench would be useless to a car mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' looks like a tool, but here it is anything that spans; the motorist cannot drive over a bridge meant for walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A footbridge is a bridge for pedestrians only, so it spans a gap but cannot carry cars.
